another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first step. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about your child(ren).

**How old is the child you're claiming for?** (Or if you have multiple children, please tell me the age of each one)

The age category is important because it affects what other conditions need to be met:
- **Under 16**: Generally have fewer requirements
- **16-19**: May qualify if they're in full-time education or certain training
- **20 or over**: Cannot qualify for Child Benefit

Please provide the age(s) of your child(ren).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi, yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and I'd like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex is 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 13 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is 13 years old (under 16), we're on track. Now I need to check another condition:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work?**

(This is mainly a formality for younger children - most 13-year-olds wouldn't be working full-time anyway, but I need to confirm this.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just in school like any other 13-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex doesn't work, so he definitely works less than 24 hours per week. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check another eligibility requirement:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?** Specifically, is Alex not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit (in their own right)

In most cases, 13-year-olds won't be receiving these, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a kid - I'm the one who handles all that sort of thing for the family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for a 13-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships. At 13 years old, this is unlikely to apply, but let me confirm:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?** 

For context, certain apprenticeships can affect eligibility depending on which country you're in (England, Scotland, or Wales). But since Alex is only 13 and still in school, I assume the answer is no - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. He's only 13 - he's just doing his normal schoolwork.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me move on to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you meet any of the following UK residency requirements?**

The main ones are:
1. **Normally live in the UK** - This is the most common path
2. **Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - If applicable
3. **Have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - With specific conditions depending on your circumstances (working, studying, jobseeking, or with sufficient resources)
4. **Living abroad as a Crown servant** - In certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation? Or to put it simply - do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK in Manchester with Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. This is about whether you're responsible for his care and upkeep.

**Do you meet any of these responsibility conditions?**

1. **You live with Alex** - You're living with him in Manchester
2. **You contribute to his upkeep** - You pay for his food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.
3. **Maintenance payments** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement

Based on what you've told me (that you're based in Manchester with Alex), it sounds like you live with him - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That confirms you live with Alex and are responsible for him. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check an important question about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else (such as the other parent, another relative, or someone else) also claiming or intending to claim Child Benefit for Alex?**

In other words:
- Is there another person who might be claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- If yes, have you both agreed who should be the claimant?
- Or is there any dispute about who should claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're the only one claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's current living situation:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- Is he living at home with you normally?
- Or is he currently in hospital for an extended period?
- Is he in local authority care?
- Is he in a fostering arrangement?

Based on what you've told me so far, I assume he's living at home with you normally in Manchester - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me - just a normal home situation, nothing complicated.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! We're almost there. Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you covering Alex's housing and upkeep costs yourself, rather than the council paying for him? This would typically be the case if he's living at home with you - but I need to confirm this for the final eligibility determination.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - I'm covering everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards Alex's care or accommodation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of information I need. You've met all the eligibility requirements. Let me now report your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility determination.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

**Great news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**. You've met all the eligibility requirements.

---

### What This Means

You can claim Child Benefit for Alex, your 13-year-old child living with you in Manchester. As the sole supporter providing for his accommodation and maintenance, and with no other claimants involved, you meet all the criteria.

---

### Next Steps

To claim Child Benefit, you should:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim or **by post using form CH2**

2. **Prepare these documents:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Proof of Alex's identity or citizenship
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to a tax charge on your Child Benefit, even though you're eligible to receive it
   - This is based on your household income

4. **Payment frequency:**
   - Child Benefit is normally paid every 4 weeks
   - As a single parent, you may be eligible for weekly payments instead (you can choose)

---

### Useful Links

- How to claim: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- More information: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?
